command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
#
# THE SCORING IS GATK4'S, VERBATIM. recipes/gatk4/02-concordance.task.json restricts both sides
# to the GIAB BED, splits multiallelics and left-aligns against the same chr20.fa, then counts
# bcftools isec. Reusing that code rather than writing a second scorer is what makes Clair3's
# F1 comparable to GATK4's 0.99272 -- a different scorer would produce a different number for
# reasons unrelated to the caller.

echo "== restrict both call set and truth to GIAB high-confidence regions =="
# -f PASS IS LOAD-BEARING. Clair3 writes a RefCall row for every position it examined and
# judged reference -- 179,453 of them here against 118,312 PASS calls. Without this filter the
# scorer treats each one as a query variant, and the "false positives" it reports are Clair3
# correctly saying "no variant here". GATK4 emits no such rows, which is exactly why the two
# call sets need different preparation before the SAME scorer can compare them.
bcftools view -R truth.chr20.bed -f PASS -Ou clair3.vcf.gz | bcftools norm -f chr20.fa -m -any -Oz -o q.vcf.gz
printf 'query_pass_only\tRefCall and LowQual rows excluded before scoring\n'
bcftools view -R truth.chr20.bed -i 'GT="alt"' -Ou truth.chr20.vcf.gz | bcftools norm -f chr20.fa -m -any -Oz -o t.vcf.gz
bcftools index -f q.vcf.gz
bcftools index -f t.vcf.gz

# EACH CALLER IS SCORED AT ITS OWN OPERATING POINT, and that is the fair comparison rather
# than the loose one. The gatk4 scorer applies QUAL>=30 to its query, which keeps ~99% of GATK's
# calls because GATK QUAL for a 36x germline sample runs into the hundreds. Clair3's QUAL is on
# a different scale entirely -- measured on this run: median 23.2, p90 31.6, and only 17.5% of
# PASS SNVs reach 30. Carrying GATK's threshold across discards 82% of Clair3's correct calls
# and reports recall 0.229 with precision 1.00000 and ZERO false positives -- the signature of
# a truncated query, not a bad caller.
#
# Clair3's own quality decision is FILTER=PASS, already applied above. So no second numeric
# gate is used here; a threshold calibrated for another tool's scale is not a fairer comparison
# than each tool's own recommended cutoff, it is just a different and wrong one. The QUAL>=30
# figure is still computed and REPORTED so the size of that effect is visible.
score(){
  ty=$1; qfile=${2:-q.vcf.gz}; tag=${3:-}
  bcftools view -v "$ty" -Oz -o q.$ty$tag.vcf.gz "$qfile"
  bcftools view -v "$ty" -Oz -o t.$ty.vcf.gz t.vcf.gz
  bcftools index -f q.$ty$tag.vcf.gz
  bcftools index -f t.$ty.vcf.gz
  rm -rf is.$ty$tag
  bcftools isec -p is.$ty$tag q.$ty$tag.vcf.gz t.$ty.vcf.gz
  FP=$(grep -vc '^#' is.$ty$tag/0000.vcf || true)
  FN=$(grep -vc '^#' is.$ty$tag/0001.vcf || true)
  TP=$(grep -vc '^#' is.$ty$tag/0002.vcf || true)
  awk -v ty="$ty" -v tp="$TP" -v fp="$FP" -v fn="$FN" 'BEGIN{
    p=(tp+fp)>0?tp/(tp+fp):0; r=(tp+fn)>0?tp/(tp+fn):0; f=(p+r)>0?2*p*r/(p+r):0;
    printf "%s_tp %d\n%s_fp %d\n%s_fn %d\n%s_precision %.5f\n%s_recall %.5f\n%s_f1 %.5f\n",
      ty,tp,ty,fp,ty,fn,ty,p,ty,r,ty,f }'
}
score snps   > snps.kv
score indels > indels.kv

# The GATK-threshold variant, computed only to show how large the scale mismatch is.
bcftools view -i 'QUAL>=30' -Oz -o q30.vcf.gz q.vcf.gz
bcftools index -f q30.vcf.gz
score snps q30.vcf.gz _q30 > snps_q30.kv
getv(){ awk -v k="$1" '$1==k{print $2}' "$2"; }

STP=$(getv snps_tp snps.kv); SFP=$(getv snps_fp snps.kv); SFN=$(getv snps_fn snps.kv)
SP=$(getv snps_precision snps.kv); SR=$(getv snps_recall snps.kv); SF=$(getv snps_f1 snps.kv)
IP=$(getv indels_precision indels.kv); IR=$(getv indels_recall indels.kv); IF1=$(getv indels_f1 indels.kv)
BEDBP=$(awk '{s+=$3-$2} END{print s}' truth.chr20.bed)
DENOM=$((STP + SFN))

printf 'benchmark_bases\t%s\n' "$BEDBP"
printf 'snv_tp\t%s\n' "$STP"
printf 'snv_fp\t%s\n' "$SFP"
printf 'snv_fn\t%s\n' "$SFN"
printf 'snv_precision\t%s\n' "$SP"
printf 'snv_recall\t%s\n' "$SR"
printf 'snv_f1\t%s\n' "$SF"
printf 'indel_precision\t%s\tOBSERVATION\n' "$IP"
printf 'indel_recall\t%s\tOBSERVATION\n' "$IR"
printf 'indel_f1\t%s\tOBSERVATION\n' "$IF1"
printf 'truth_side_snv_denominator\t%s\n' "$DENOM"
Q30R=$(awk '$1=="snps_recall"{print $2}' snps_q30.kv)
Q30P=$(awk '$1=="snps_precision"{print $2}' snps_q30.kv)
printf 'snv_recall_at_gatk_qual30\t%s\tREPORTED: GATK threshold on Clair3 scale\n' "$Q30R"
printf 'snv_precision_at_gatk_qual30\t%s\tREPORTED\n' "$Q30P"

# ---------------------------------------------------------- the cross-recipe identity
# TP + FN is the truth-side SNV count inside the BED -- a property of the TRUTH SET and the
# region, not of the caller. gatk4-real measured 69,210 on the identical files. If Clair3's
# denominator matches, both recipes are scored against the same truth variants and their F1s
# are comparable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by assumption. If it differs, the comparison is
# meaningless no matter how good the F1 looks.
printf 'gatk4_denominator\t69210\n'
test "$DENOM" = "69210" || {
  echo "FAIL: truth-side SNV denominator $DENOM != gatk4's 69210; the two recipes are not"
  echo "      scoring against the same truth set, so their F1 values are not comparable"
  exit 1; }
printf 'identity_denominator\tsame truth-side SNV set as gatk4 (69,210)\n'
printf 'gatk4_snv_f1\t0.99272\tfor side-by-side reading, not asserted here\n'

# Floors justified the same way gatk4's are: this recipe applies no variant filtering beyond
# QUAL>=30, so precision is partly a property of the recipe rather than of Clair3, and a floor
# sitting 0.001 under the observed value would fail on noise.
awk -v p="$SP" 'BEGIN{ if (p+0 < 0.97) { printf "FAIL: SNV precision %s below the 0.97 floor\n", p; exit 1 } }' || exit 1
awk -v r="$SR" 'BEGIN{ if (r+0 < 0.98) { printf "FAIL: SNV recall %s below the 0.98 floor\n", r; exit 1 } }' || exit 1
awk -v f="$SF" 'BEGIN{ if (f+0 < 0.975) { printf "FAIL: SNV F1 %s below the 0.975 floor\n", f; exit 1 } }' || exit 1
printf 'concordance\tClair3 SNVs scored against GIAB HG001 v4.2.1 inside its confident regions\n'

# Indels REPORTED, not asserted -- POS:REF:ALT equality after left-alignment still counts two
# correct spellings of one indel as FP *and* FN, which hap.py's haplotype comparison credits.
# Asserting it would assert a representation difference. Same decision as gatk4.

{ printf 'observable\tvalue\n'
  printf 'benchmark_bases\t%s\n' "$BEDBP"
  printf 'snv_tp\t%s\nsnv_fp\t%s\nsnv_fn\t%s\n' "$STP" "$SFP" "$SFN"
  printf 'snv_precision\t%s\nsnv_recall\t%s\nsnv_f1\t%s\n' "$SP" "$SR" "$SF"
  printf 'indel_precision\t%s\nindel_recall\t%s\nindel_f1\t%s\n' "$IP" "$IR" "$IF1"
  printf 'truth_side_snv_denominator\t%s\n' "$DENOM"
Q30R=$(awk '$1=="snps_recall"{print $2}' snps_q30.kv)
Q30P=$(awk '$1=="snps_precision"{print $2}' snps_q30.kv)
printf 'snv_recall_at_gatk_qual30\t%s\tREPORTED: GATK threshold on Clair3 scale\n' "$Q30R"
printf 'snv_precision_at_gatk_qual30\t%s\tREPORTED\n' "$Q30P"
  printf 'gatk4_snv_f1\t0.99272\n'; } > score.tsv
cp score.tsv clair3-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "CLAIR3 CONCORDANCE OK"
